description:
The OSD campaign's bit-error stopping rule and bit-level Clopper-Pearson BER intervals assume independent bit trials, but decoder failures produce correlated bit-error bursts, making every recorded BER interval roughly three times too narrow.

## Background

Each cell stops on a cumulative information-bit-error target (default 100), which a cell reaches from only seven to nine failed blocks at twelve to sixteen bit errors per failure. The independent sampling unit is the block; the recorded interval treats sampled bits as independent trials. Recorded intervals span roughly +/-19% of the estimate, while the independent-failure count supports roughly +/-70%. In the eBCH(128,64) reference campaign this flipped three of four published-point rejections when re-evaluated with a block-resolved interval derived from the receipt's own BLER interval, and the order-1 control arm shows non-monotone point estimates whose recorded intervals cannot resolve published values differing by a factor of three. The recorded BLER interval is unaffected (it is computed over blocks).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Cell stopping targets a count of independent error events (block errors), or the recorded BER interval uses an estimator valid under within-block error clustering (for example a clustered or ratio interval over block failures).
- [hard] REQ-02: The receipt names the sampling unit and estimator for every interval it records, and the BER interval's stated coverage is valid under the block-burst error process.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test exercises a bursty-error decoder fixture and verifies the recorded BER interval widens relative to the bit-independence interval.
- [hard] REQ-04: Existing committed receipts remain readable; reinterpretation of their recorded intervals is documented rather than silently rewritten.
title: campaign BER intervals assume bit independence under block-burst errors
